events.summary: First-cut signage for Dypsis pembana, drawn primarily from IUCN Red List data (via Wikipedia/Wikidata), NCBI peer-reviewed research, HEAR/PACSOA assessment, Palmpedia, and Florida nursery cultivation notes. Confidence is high on range, IUCN status, morphology, and general cultivation; lower on precise bloom timing (omitted), wildlife interactions in Florida (genus-level inference only), and edibility/toxicity (no D. pembana-specific data found — extrapolated from congener D. lutescens ASPCA records).

events.summary: Applied all five reviewer directives: reordered quick_hits and more_information per stated priority, added the self-cleaning trunk feature throughout (stems block, what_to_look_for, size habit, growing_conditions spacing), and added a hedged cold-hardiness note to size/growth_rate. The reviewer's 28°F–30°F figure could not be confirmed against authoritative sources — sources ranged widely and conflicted — so the note cites demonstrated field performance in inland Sarasota County (Palmpedia/Fairchild Garden) and flags Zone 9b microclimate possibility without asserting a precise temperature floor.

events.feedback:
Yes — **this is shaping up very well**. Of the four palm entries you've shown me recently, I think the Pemba Palm is among the strongest conceptually: it has a very clear visual identity, a genuinely unusual geographic story, conservation significance, and useful “look for this” information.

I would, however, make a handful of corrections/tightenings. I also found **one particularly good story you should absolutely keep**, plus one taxonomy issue worth handling carefully.

**Readability:** 8.5/10

**Field usefulness:** 9/10
